translations.text: Again, the first song of praise of Moses.
Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song of praise to the Lord and said: “Let us praise the exalted Lord, who has triumphed over the horses and their riders and thrown them into the sea.”
The mighty and praiseworthy Lord has shone forth and become our Savior. This is my God, and I will praise him; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.
The Lord is mighty and a warrior; the Lord is his name.
He threw Pharaoh’s chariots and his army into the sea, and he drowned his chosen warriors in the Red Sea.
The depths covered them; they went down into the deep and sank like stones.
Your right hand, Lord, is glorious in power; your right hand, Lord, shattered your enemies.
In your great might you overthrew those who hate you. You sent out your anger, and it consumed them like stubble.
At the breath of your nostrils the waters piled up. The flowing waters stood like waterskins; the depths congealed in the heart of the sea.
The enemy said, “I will pursue, I will overtake, and I will divide the plunder. My appetite will devour them. I will draw my sword, and my hand will destroy them.”
You blew your wind, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
Who is like you, Lord? Who is like you, majestic in holiness, awe-inspiring and praiseworthy, working wonders?
You raised your right hand, and the earth swallowed them.
In your kindness you led this people whom you redeemed. In your might you led them to your holy dwelling.
The nations heard and trembled, and fear seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
Then the chiefs of Edom were afraid, and trembling seized the warriors of Moab. All the inhabitants of Canaan were shattered.
May fear and trembling fall upon them. By the greatness of your arm, may they sink like stones, until your people pass through, Lord, until this people whom you redeemed passes through.
You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance. You made a place ready for your dwelling, Lord—your sanctuary, Lord, which you established with your hands.
The Lord will reign forever and ever.
For Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, and the Lord brought the waters of the sea back over them. But the Israelites walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea.
Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and drums.
Miriam sang in response to them: “Praise the exalted Lord, who has triumphed over the horses and their riders and thrown them into the sea.”
The second song of praise of Moses.
Listen, heavens, and I will speak. Let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
May my teaching fall like rain, and my words descend like dew, like breezes upon tender grass and like showers upon vegetation.
For I will call on the name of the Lord. Ascribe greatness to our God.
The Mighty One’s works are without defect, and all his ways are just. He is a faithful God, without injustice, righteous and upright.
They have acted corruptly; they are not his children, but blemished children, a crooked and twisted generation.
Is this how you repay the Lord, foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father, who acquired you? He is the one who made you and established you.
Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will show you; ask your elders, and they will tell you.
When the Most High divided the nations, when he separated humankind, he established the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the Israelites.
For the Lord’s portion is his people, and Jacob is his allotted inheritance.
He found him in a desert land, in a desolate wasteland. He surrounded him, cherished him, and guarded him like the pupil of an eye.
Like an eagle flying over its nest and hovering over its young, he spread his wings, received them, and carried them on his strong pinions.
The Lord alone led him, and no foreign god was with him.
He settled him on the heights of the earth and fed him the produce of the field. He gave him honey to suck from the rock, and oil from flinty rock.
Curds from cattle and milk from sheep, with the fat of fattened animals—rams, offspring of [?], and goats—together with the rich fat of wheat; and he gave him the blood of grapes, wine, to drink.
Israel grew fat and kicked. He grew fat and strong and acquired possessions. He forgot the God who made him and reviled the Mighty One who redeemed him.
He made him jealous with foreign gods and angered him with idols.
They sacrificed to demons that were not gods, to gods they had not known, new ones that had only now been made, whom your ancestors had not feared.
You forgot the Mighty One who fathered you, and you were unmindful of the God who glorified you.
The Lord saw and became angry, because his sons and daughters had provoked him.
He said, “I will turn my face away from them and see what their end will be, for they are a perverse generation, children with no faithfulness in them.”

“They made me jealous with what is not God and angered me with the things they worship. I too will make them jealous through those who are not my people, and I will anger them through a foolish nation.”
“For a fire is kindled in my anger and burns down to the lowest Sheol. It will consume the earth and its produce and set the foundations of the mountains on fire.”
I will heap disasters upon them and use up my arrows against them.

They will be ravaged by hunger, and evil spirits will be unleashed upon them. He handed them over to the birds. I will stir up fanged beasts against them, along with the venom of snakes that crawl in the dust.
Outside, the sword will cut them down, and inside the chambers, terror: soldiers and virgins alike, and children along with old men.
I said, “Where are they? I will erase their memory from among humanity.”
Were it not for the enemy's rage, which had grown strong, lest their enemies exalt themselves and say, “Our own hand has prevailed; it was not the Lord who did all this.”
For they are a people whose judgment is lost, and there is no understanding among them.
If only they were wise and understood this, and considered their end!
One would chase a thousand, and two would put ten thousand to flight, unless their Mighty One had handed them over and the Lord had confined them.
For their strength was not like our strength, and our enemies are judges.
For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom and from the planting of Gomorrah. Their grapes are bitter grapes, and their clusters bring them bitterness.
Their venom is the venom of a dragon and the deadly poison of an asp.
Look, it is hidden away with me and sealed in the treasuries.
Vengeance is mine; I will repay them when their foot slips. For the day of their destruction is near, and what awaits them is coming quickly.
For the Lord will judge his people and relent concerning his servants, because he has seen that a hand has prevailed and there is no one to help or support them.
And I said, “Where are their gods, the mighty ones in whom they trusted,
Those who used to eat the fat of their sacrifices and drink the wine of their drink offerings—let them rise now and help you, and let them shelter you.
See, then, that I am he, and there is no God apart from me. I put to death, and I bring to life. I wound, and I heal. No one can escape from my hands.
For I raised my hand toward heaven and said, ‘I live forever.
I will sharpen the edge of my sword like lightning, and my hand will take hold of judgment. I will bring vengeance upon those who hate me and repay my enemies.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh: the blood of the slain and the captives, and flesh from the enemy's crowned head.
Now, nations, praise his people, for he avenges the blood of his servants. He brings vengeance upon those who hate him and makes atonement for his land and his people.
The Song of Isaiah.

Let the heavens rejoice above, and let the clouds sprinkle righteousness. Let the earth open, let salvation abound, and let righteousness spring up together with it. I am the Lord, who created these things.
Sing a new song to the Lord, his praise from the ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea, with all that fills it, the islands and those who live in them.
Let the wilderness and its towns rejoice, and let Kedar become meadows. Let those who live among the cliffs sing praise, and let them shout from the mountaintops.
Let them give praise to the Lord and proclaim his praises in the islands.
The Lord will go out like a mighty warrior, and like a man of war he will stir up zeal. He will shout, show his might, and kill his enemies.
The Song of Hannah.
My heart has grown strong in the Lord, and my horn has been raised high in God my Savior. My mouth has opened against my enemies, because you have made me rejoice in your salvation.
There is no one holy like the Lord, and no one strong like our God, for there is no one besides him.
Do not keep speaking boastful words, and let no oppression come from your mouths, for the Lord is knowledge, and schemes cannot stand before him.
The bows of the mighty will be broken, and the weak have been strengthened with power.

Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread, and those who were hungry have become prosperous. The barren woman has given birth and is satisfied, while the woman with many children has become desolate.
The Lord puts to death and brings to life. He brings down to Sheol and raises up.
The Lord makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and also raises up.
He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the wretched from the rubbish heap, to seat them with the leaders of the people and give them a throne of honor as their inheritance.
He hears the prayer of everyone who prays to him and blesses the years of the righteous, for a mighty man does not prevail by his own strength.

The Lord will shatter those who provoke him and thunder against them in heaven. Let the wise man not boast in his wisdom, nor the mighty man in his might, nor the rich man in his riches. Rather, let whoever boasts boast in this: that he understands and knows me, that I am the Lord, who acts with kindness, righteousness, and justice on earth. The Lord will judge the ends of the earth, give strength to its kings, and raise high the horn of his anointed one.
The Song of Habakkuk.

Lord, I heard the report of you and was afraid. Lord, I saw your works and was amazed. Between two living creatures you will be known. In the midst of the years you will reveal yourself, and when the time draws near you will appear. In wrath, remember your mercy.
God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. The heavens were covered by the splendor of the Glorious One, and the earth was filled with his praise.
His radiance will be like light. In the [?] of his hands he will place his strength in [?].
The word will go before him, and discipline will go out at his feet.
He stood, and the earth shook. He looked, and the nations melted away. The ancient mountains melted, and the everlasting hills were brought low. His are the ways of old.
The tents of the Cushites will be stretched out, and the tent curtains of Midian will tremble.
Were you angry with the rivers, Lord? Was your anger against the rivers, and your fury against the sea? You rode on horses and on the chariot of salvation.
Your bow will surely be drawn, Lord, against the dominion of kingdoms. The earth will be plowed with rivers.
The nations will see it and writhe like a woman giving birth. The deep raised its voice and lifted its hands high.
The sun and moon stood still in their dwellings. They move by the light of your arrows and by the gleaming flashes of your spears.
In your fury you will march over the earth, and in your anger you will thresh the nations.
You went out to save your people and to save your anointed one. You cut off the head from the house of the wicked, and stripped it bare from its foundations up to its neck forever.
You pierced the head of his rulers with a staff. They trusted in their arrogance that they would devour the poor in secret.
You rode through the sea on horses, through the mass of mighty waters.
I heard, and my belly trembled at the utterance of my lips. Trembling entered my bones, and my knees shook, because he revealed to me and showed me the day of distress that is coming upon the people.

For the fig tree has not budded, and there are no leaves on the vine. The olive's fruit has failed, and the threshing floors have produced no grain. The sheep have vanished from the fold, and there are no cattle in the herds.
But I will rejoice in the Lord and be glad in God my Savior.
The Lord of lords is my strength. He made my feet like a deer's and set me on the heights, so that I might sing his praises.
The Song of Isaiah.
At night my soul longs for you; my spirit within me also seeks you early. For according to your judgments on the earth, the inhabitants of the world have learned righteousness.
Let the evildoer be removed, so that he does not learn righteousness, and let rebuke be established in the land. Let the wicked be taken away, so that he does not see the glory of the Lord.
Lord, they will not see when your hands are raised high. They will see your zeal for your people and be ashamed. Like a furnace, you will devour them, your enemies.
Lord, preserve peace for us, for you have made provision for us according to all our deeds.
Lord our God, take us as your own, for masters other than you have ruled over us. Your name alone will we remember.
The dead do not live, and the mighty do not rise. Therefore you visited them, destroyed them, and wiped out all memory of them.
You have increased your people, Lord; you have increased your people. You withdrew and drove away all the wicked of the earth.
Lord, in distress they sought you, and in confinement they whispered of your discipline.
Like a pregnant woman who is close to giving birth, who writhes and cries out in her labor pains, so we were before you, Lord.
We conceived and suffered labor pains like women who give birth to wind. Save us, so that we do not perish on the earth and the inhabitants of the world do not fall.
The dead will live, and their bodies will rise. Those who sleep in the dust will wake and sing praise, for your dew is a dew of light. You will overthrow the land of the wicked.
The Song of Jonah.
I called to the Lord in my distress, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried out, and you heard my voice.
You cast me into the depths, into the heart of the sea, and the currents surrounded me. All your breakers and waves passed over me.
Then I said, 'I have been driven far from your sight. Yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'
The waters surrounded me up to my throat, and the deep encircled me. My head was imprisoned at the bottom of the sea.
I went down to the foundations of the mountains, and the earth shut its bars before me forever. But you brought my life up from destruction, Lord my God.
When my soul grew faint, I remembered the Lord, and my prayer came before you, into your holy temple.
All who cling to worthless objects of worship abandon your mercy.
But I will sacrifice to you with a voice of thanksgiving, and I will fulfill what I have vowed. Repayment belongs to the Lord.
The Song of Hananiah and His Companions.
Blessed are you, Lord, God of our ancestors, and your name is exalted and praised forever.
For you are righteous in everything you have done to us. All your deeds are true, your ways are upright, and all your judgments are trustworthy.

For you have dealt with us in true judgment in everything you brought upon us and upon the holy city of our ancestors, Jerusalem. For you brought all these things upon us justly, because of our offenses and sins.
For we have sinned and acted wickedly before you. We have turned away from you and transgressed your word, and we have sinned against you.
We have neither obeyed nor kept your commandments, nor have we done as you commanded us so that it might go well with us.
Everything you have done to us and everything you have brought upon us, you have done to us in just judgment.
You handed us over to our enemies, lawless people who are far from you, and to the rule of a wicked kingdom, worse than all the kingdoms of the earth.
And now, Lord, we have no way to open our mouths before you, because of the shame and disgrace that have come upon your servants and those who fear you.
For your name’s sake, do not give us up completely, and do not cancel your covenant.
Do not take your mercy and kindness away from us, for the sake of Abraham your friend, Isaac your servant, and Israel your holy one.
to whom you promised that you would multiply their descendants like the stars in heaven and like the sand on the seashore.
And now, Lord, see how we have been brought lower than all the nations, and today we are scattered throughout the earth because of our offenses and sins.
At this time there is no chief, ruler, prophet, or leader, no altar, sacrifice, or offering, and no place to offer incense or a sacrifice and find favor and mercy.
But with a broken heart and a humble spirit, here we are, offered up to the burning fire.
We ask that the offering of ourselves before you today may be worth more than bulls, rams, and many lambs. Let your servants not be put to shame, for those who trust in you are not put to shame.
And now we follow you wholeheartedly, and we seek your face, Lord.
Do not put us to shame, but deal with us according to your abundant kindness and your great mercy.
Save us according to your many wonders, and bring glory to your name, Lord.
Let all those who speak evil against your servants be put to shame. Let them be put to shame despite all their might, and let their strength desert them.
Let them know that you alone are the one God, and that you are praised in all your works.
Those who were heating the fiery furnace did not stop, but kept throwing into it naphtha, pitch, sulfur, reeds, and vine branches.
The flame of fire roared and rose forty-nine cubits above the fiery furnace.
The fire burned up and destroyed everyone it found around the furnace, both Chaldeans and accusers.
But the angel of the Lord went down into the fiery furnace with Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, and extinguished the fiery flame in the furnace.
He made the middle of the furnace like a dew-laden breeze. The fire did not come near them at all, nor did it hurt or distress them.
Then all three, as though speaking with one mouth, praised and blessed God from inside the fiery furnace, saying:
Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers. You are praised and exalted forever. Blessed is the holy name of your glory. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you in your holy temple. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you who sit enthroned upon the cherubim and look upon the depths. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you on your royal throne. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you in the vault of heaven. You are praised and exalted forever.
The prayer of Hananiah and his companions.
All you works of the Lord, bless the Lord. Praise and exalt him forever.
And you angels of the Lord, bless the Lord.
Bless, you heavens.
Bless, you waters above the heavens.
And all you hosts of the Lord, bless the Lord.
Bless, you sun and moon.
And all you stars in the sky, bless the Lord.
Bless, you rain and dew.
And all you winds, bless the Lord.
Bless the Lord, you fire and heat.
Bless, you cold and heat.
You snow and ice, bless the Lord.
Bless, you night and day.
You light and darkness, bless the Lord.
Bless the Lord, you lightning and clouds.
Bless, you earth.
And you mountains and hills.
And everything that grows on the earth, bless the Lord.
And all you springs of water, bless the Lord.
Bless, you seas and rivers.
Bless the Lord, you fish and everything that moves in the waters.
Bless, all you birds of the sky.
And you wild animals, bless the Lord.
And all you human beings, bless the Lord.
Bless, you people of the house of Israel.
Bless, you priests.
Servants of the Lord, the Lord.
Bless, you spirits and souls of the righteous.
You blameless and humble in heart, the Lord.

Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, bless the Lord. Apostles and prophets, martyrs and confessors, bless the Lord. All who stand in the house of the Lord, bless the Lord. We bless the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. We praise and exalt them forever.
The Prayer of Hezekiah.
I said, “In the middle of my days I am departing. At the gate of Sheol I have left the remainder of my years.”
I said, “I will not see the Lord in the land of the living, nor will I see people again among the inhabitants of the grave.”

My dwelling has been taken away and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent. My life has been rolled up like a weaver’s work, like a web about to be cut off. From day until night you brought me to an end.
Like a chirping swallow I chirped, and like a dove I moaned. I lifted my eyes to the heights. Lord, rescue me and restore me.
What shall I say? He spoke to me, and he passed by and disturbed all my sleep because of the bitterness of my soul. Lord, by these things they will live.
For these are the life of my spirit. Restore my health and give me life.
Look, instead of peace I experienced bitter suffering. But you took delight in my life, so that it would not waste away in destruction, for you have thrown all my sins behind your back.
For Sheol will not thank you, nor will death praise you. Those who go down to the pit will not hope in your faithfulness.
Rather, the living will give you thanks, as I do today. A father will make your faithfulness known to his children.
The Lord will save me, and we will sing his praises all the days of our lives in the house of the Lord...
The Song of Praise of David.
My God, you are my God; I wait for you. My soul thirsts for you, and my flesh longs for you, like a thirsty, exhausted land that seeks water.
So I have looked upon you in truth, to see your strength and your glory.
For your mercy is better than my life, and my lips will praise you.
So I will bless you throughout my life, and in your name I will lift up my hands.
My soul will be nourished as with oil and fat, and my mouth will praise you with lips of praise.
I remembered you on my bed, and during the nights I meditated on you.
For you have been my helper, and in the shadow of your wings I will glory.
My soul followed after you, and your right hand supported me.
They sought to destroy my life, but they will enter the depths of the earth.
They will be handed over to the sword and become food for foxes.
The king will rejoice in God, and everyone who swears by him will boast, for the mouths of liars will be shut.
